transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the August 25 production policy review for the public API rate-limit project, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the process. I'll be making the final decision on the policy that gets communicated to customers, but before I do, I need each of your teams — backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations — to report your release-impacting findings. To get us started, here's where the draft policy currently stands: 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, the same limit applied to authentication endpoints, and no specified staffed launch window. I'd like to hear from each of you on whether you see any issues or concerns with these parameters before I record the final policy.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a release-impacting finding from backend engineering. While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Our load replay confirms the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. I hadn't updated the draft because the client test was owned by another team, but this directly affects the proposed 100 requests per minute limit — it would break legitimate customer workflows.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from customer success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that Acme's contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered the clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this contractual notice requirement needs to be factored into our rollout timeline and policy communication.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. This directly conflicts with the draft policy's current plan to apply the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints — that limit would be far too permissive and would leave us exposed to credential-stuffing attacks. The finding isn't in the security tracker yet because the investigation is still being closed, but this needs to be factored into the final policy before it's recorded.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from support operations. We confirmed today that the staffed launch team is available only from exactly 10:00 to 12:00 UTC on September 15, with an escalation handoff documented for that window. I haven't added the coverage block to the launch plan yet because scheduling approval finished after the plan was circulated, but this is our only available staffed launch window and it needs to be factored into the final policy and rollout timeline.
transcript.speaker: A5
